reason: Re-opened Sastri's Sankara via packet.js gita 15 --verse 15.7: both evidence pieces are there verbatim at 15.7 (the jalasurya simile, the reflected sun returning to the original sun on removal of the water, and the answer to the objection that the partless Self has no parts: a portion limited by the upadhi of avidya, a portion as it were, an imaginary portion). The 15.6 commentary ends with the question of how those reaching the abode do not return, which 15.7 answers, so the plain sense's hinge (abode whence none return, then the soul in the body) matches the day's text (15.6, 15.7 to 15.11) without doctrine. verse: verse.js ok, ref 15.7, at 556, the natural key for this reading; Telang 'an eternal portion of me' confirms nothing rests on Besant-only wording. attribution: Sankara's own bhasya (the Sanskrit amsa iva kalpitah / jalasuryaka image), not Sastri's inserted headings. drift: 'only in imagination' carries 'as it were, an imaginary portion'; 'returns to the sun once the water is removed' carries the simile; the jar-space alternative is omitted, not contradicted. school named (Advaita), not required with one name but not wrong. No comparison, no tone issue. form: entry-check ok, 45 words at the cap, one semicolon, verb 'reads', roster spelling, no dash. No attack lands.
